Reduce a blocker to its smallest reproduction, establish whether it is a defect or a design decision, and file it upstream with the reproduction. Filing defects is a contribution; filing requests is not.

```day-atom
{"in":["language-fact"],"out":["filed-gap"],"next":["rfc-draft"]}
```

G14: a loop has no diverge exemption, so an intentionally infinite loop needs a false measure. A recursive fn may decline to prove termination by declaring fx diverge, and the checker names the exemption itself; taking it costs assurance rather than being free, dropping the item from L3 to L1. The exemption does not reach loops: a loop requires dec even when the enclosing function declares fx diverge, so an idle loop is only writable by supplying dec 0, a measure that cannot strictly decrease, which then sits in the source where a later reader will believe it. Not a gap by contrast: spec fn requires a measure with no exemption, recursive or not, which is correct because a non-total spec function would be unsound. Scope: small, extend the exemption from functions to the loops inside them.

G12 does not invalidate the extension RFC set. It is not a semantics gap: equivalent-mutants.md OQ-1 states the formulation already generalises, with the spec-fn pair returning the wrapper type and ensuring its ==, and only the scalar arm grounded. So it is an unimplemented arm with a written design, the same class as G4. It touches no surface and no proposal depends on it. What it blocks is the evidence rather than the design: while it stands, no step-shaped subsystem can be shown meeting the section 7 floor, because step : State x Event -> State x Action returns a struct by construction, so every transition Bulla intends to write is in the affected class.

Item 4 of the spec-surface report was recorded with the wrong error and is not a separate defect. It was 'a spec closure does not elaborate in value position' with error[E0308] expected FnSpec<(u32,), bool> found closure. Re-running it at the pin gives error[E0308] mismatched types, expected Seq<u32> found TVecU32 - the closure is not the problem, the receiver is. A combinator in value position wants a Seq and gets the bounded wrapper, which is the same missing bridge as item 2's 'no method named view found for struct TVecU64'. So items 2 and 4 are one defect with two symptoms and one fix, and the report goes from four items to three, each with a located fix in a different file: the nat classifier in thermite-lower, the wrapper's missing View, and the combinator collection walk's missing ADT arm. Reproduced all three at the pin rather than transcribing them, which is what surfaced the wrong error.

The spec-surface defects are filed upstream as three issues rather than one report: Thermite#124 (a spec fn over an ADT has its declared bool return rewritten to nat), #125 (the bounded Vec wrapper has no View, so spec positions needing a Seq fail), #126 (combinators are not collected from a struct inv). Three rather than four because items 2 and 4 were one defect with two symptoms, and three rather than one because each fix is in a different file - the shape classifier in thermite-lower, the wrapper emitter, and the combinator collection walk. Each carries a reproduction run at the pin, the mechanism with a file and line, a suggested fix, and the environment. #124 leads with a non-recursive reproduction because that is what shows the previously recorded diagnosis was wrong.
